chapter: Early bands and the Fritz family in Mandeville
title: Why Lewis lived in Mandeville and moved back to New Orleans
summary: His daughter's fever sent him to the north shore, where he joined Black Eagle's band and Leonard Parker's. He commuted weekly to New Orleans before moving back.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: No, you see, my family and I, we were minding a club, and regalese, and I was a club, and regalese, you know? And uh, my oldest daughter, Mildred, she was a small child, she was taken with terrible fever from mosquito bites, and the doctor ordered me to take her, thought probably she had some lung trouble or something, to bring her over there in his party. But my father was over in that neighborhood, so I just brought her. Well I joined the Black Eagles band, and I played with Leonard Parker, and uh, uh, Fritz played a while with Buddy Petit and he gave it up, quit the band because he was in the business of a brick, brick mason. So I joined Buddy Petit's band, not either, Edmund Hall got in the Buddy Petit's band, and I stayed with Leonard Parker. So when uh, Edmund Hall left him, and they wanted to bring uh, Isidore Fritz over, he wouldn't leave him, he never did want to come to the New Orleans. Who was it, was it the Brick Mason? Isidore Fritz. They were brick, yeah they were all bricklayers. Bricklayers. Yeah, that was my trade. And so I came on over with uh, well I'd come over week, every week, around Wednesday, and I'd stay with my mother and go back on Monday or whatever date, you know, the job would be over with. And then I just decided to move back here, but all the way they lived right here would cause me to go to that neighborhood instead of coming back to New Orleans on account of uh, Mirit being sick, yeah.
